title: Activating ZTC changes from Terraform: the activation resource and the ztcActivator CLI
aliases: ztc changes not activated after apply

prose.text: Cloud and Branch Connector stages every change until it is activated, and the ZTC provider offers two ways to do that from a Terraform workflow. {{two-ways}}

prose.label: The resource.
prose.text: What `ztc_activation_status` sends and why it never forces activation is in [[cloud-connector.api.activation-wire]] and [[shared.activation.cbc]]. {{resource-activates-only-on-create}} In legacy mode its read fails: [[cloud-connector.sdk-go.service-defects]].

prose.label: The CLI.
prose.text: {{cli-build}} {{cli-env-vars}} {{cli-cloud-optional-0-1-9}} {{cli-no-private-key}} {{cli-env-names-differ}} The guide describes credential sources the code does not read {{divergence:cli-credential-sources}}.

checks.do: Whether the activation resource was created or replaced in this apply; if it was already in state and unchanged, the apply did not activate.
For the CLI in legacy mode, that ZTW_USERNAME, ZTW_PASSWORD, ZTW_API_KEY and ZTW_CLOUD are set, not only the ZTC_* variables the provider reads.

two-ways.statement: The provider documentation says the ZTC platform requires every configuration to be activated, and offers an out-of-band CLI (ztcActivator) or the `ztc_activation_status` resource for it.

quotes: The ZTC platform requires every configuration to be activated.
or leverage the dedicated activation resource `ztc_activation_status`.
made available a dedicated out of band CLI method described here [ztc activator](guides/ztc-activator-overview.md)

resource-activates-only-on-create.statement: Because the resource activates only in its create function and every settable argument forces replacement, an apply activates only when `ztc_activation_status` is created or replaced. Once it is in state, a later apply that changes other ZTC resources does not activate unless the status read back from the API differs from the configured arguments and forces a replacement.
resource-activates-only-on-create.conditions: Follows from the resource's lifecycle functions and ForceNew arguments; not run. Which status values the API reports after an apply, and therefore whether a replacement is planned, is not shown by any source.

cli-build.statement: The ztcActivator CLI is built from the provider repository with `make ztcActivator`, which installs the binary in /usr/local/bin (C:\Windows\System32 on Windows); the guide shows it run after `terraform apply`.

cli-env-vars.statement: The CLI chooses legacy mode when `ZSCALER_USE_LEGACY_CLIENT` is `true`. In legacy mode it exits unless `ZTW_USERNAME`, `ZTW_PASSWORD`, `ZTW_API_KEY` and `ZTW_CLOUD` are set; otherwise it requires `ZSCALER_CLIENT_ID`, `ZSCALER_CLIENT_SECRET` and `ZSCALER_VANITY_DOMAIN`, with `ZSCALER_CLOUD` optional. It then calls the normal `UpdateActivationStatus`.

cli-cloud-optional-0-1-9.statement: Provider release 0.1.9 made `ZSCALER_CLOUD` optional for `ztcActivator`'s OneAPI startup; unset, it uses the default production cloud.

quotes: Updated `ztcActivator` OneAPI startup so `ZSCALER_CLOUD` is optional (unset uses the default production cloud).

cli-no-private-key.statement: The CLI's OneAPI mode authenticates only with a client secret: it never reads `ZSCALER_PRIVATE_KEY`, so a deployment that authenticates the provider with a private key cannot run the CLI with the same credentials.
cli-no-private-key.conditions: Absence: cli/ztcActivator.go was read in full at the pin; it reads no private-key variable and sets no private-key option.

cli-env-names-differ.statement: The CLI's legacy variables are named ZTW_* while the provider's legacy mode reads ZTC_*, so an environment prepared for the provider's legacy mode does not satisfy the CLI.
cli-env-names-differ.conditions: Comparison of the variable names in cli/ztcActivator.go and ztc/config.go at the pin; not run.

cli-credential-sources.summary: The activator guide says credentials can come from CLI arguments (highest priority) or environment variables; the CLI code reads only environment variables.

positions.says: Credentials can be given as CLI arguments or environment variables, with CLI arguments taking priority.

quotes: The authentication credentials can be given multiple ways, and if all are present then this is the order, from highest to lowest priority:

positions.says: Every credential is read from an environment variable, and a missing required one ends the program; the file parses no command-line arguments.

quotes: func getEnvVarOrFail(k string) string { if v := os.Getenv(k); v != "" { return v }

cli-credential-sources.impact: Passing credentials as flags, as the guide suggests, has no effect; the CLI still exits for a missing environment variable.

resolution.note: The CLI source is what runs.
